provenance.title: WHO maternal near-miss identification criteria
provenance.primarySource: WHO, Evaluating the quality of care for severe pregnancy complications: the WHO near-miss approach for maternal health (2011)
provenance.why: A maternal near-miss is a woman who nearly died but survived a complication during pregnancy, childbirth or within 42 days of termination of pregnancy. Near-misses outnumber deaths by roughly an order of magnitude, so they carry far more learning per unit of time — and unlike a death, the woman is alive to be asked what happened. Identifying them is what makes the near-miss-to-death ratio and the mortality index computable, and those two indicators say something a maternal mortality ratio cannot: whether women who reach severe complications are surviving them.
provenance.scope: IDENTIFICATION ONLY. This pack answers 'did this woman meet WHO near-miss criteria?' — a clinical classification computed from organ-dysfunction markers. It does NOT conduct a review. The confidential, no-blame REVIEW instrument (MPDSR) is specified separately and is deliberately not built here; see docs/clinical-governance/rmnp/mpdsr-review-contract.md.
provenance.notConfidential: Near-miss identification is ordinary clinical classification and carries NO confidentiality stamp. Only the review is a governed confidential instrument. Conflating the two would put a survival statistic behind a confidentiality grant and make the indicator uncomputable.

sourceVerification.note: Transcribed from the WHO near-miss approach (2011), which has no SMART DAK — like MEC, SPR and the Labour Care Guide, it is published guidance encoded and cited, not machine-readable content ingested. Every criterion names the organ system and the published threshold it encodes so ratification is a comparison rather than a rewrite.

tiers.name: Cardiovascular dysfunction
tiers.action: Cardiovascular organ dysfunction — WHO near-miss criteria met. Record as a maternal near-miss and raise the review task.

tiers.name: Respiratory dysfunction
tiers.action: Respiratory organ dysfunction — WHO near-miss criteria met.

tiers.name: Renal dysfunction
tiers.action: Renal organ dysfunction — WHO near-miss criteria met.

tiers.name: Coagulation / haematological dysfunction
tiers.action: Coagulation or haematological dysfunction — WHO near-miss criteria met.

tiers.name: Hepatic dysfunction
tiers.action: Hepatic organ dysfunction — WHO near-miss criteria met.

tiers.name: Neurological dysfunction
tiers.action: Neurological organ dysfunction — WHO near-miss criteria met.

tiers.name: Uterine dysfunction
tiers.action: Uterine dysfunction — hysterectomy for infection or haemorrhage. WHO near-miss criteria met.

tiers.name: WHO near-miss criteria not met
tiers.action: No organ-dysfunction criterion was met on the information recorded. This is NOT a statement that the woman was well — a severe maternal outcome can be present without a recorded criterion, and an unrecorded observation is not a negative one. Where any criterion is unresolved the engine returns INDETERMINATE rather than reaching this row.

testCases.name: creatinine at the published renal threshold is a near-miss
five units transfused is a near-miss; the threshold is inclusive
four units transfused alone is not, so the threshold is real and not a rubber stamp
a respiratory rate of 4 is a near-miss — the low bound is not forgotten
gasping alone is a near-miss, and it is a clinician's observation not a number
